 Scientists invent electric comb that restores hair growth ‘nearly 100%’
 Researchers say Detangle system could treat androgenetic alopecia, also known as male-pattern baldness
 Anthony Cuthbertson Tuesday 17 November 2026 23:24 EST

 Scientists in China have invented a new type of comb that stimulates rapid hair regrowth and can help reverse baldness .
 Researchers claim the electronic comb, dubbed ‘Detangle’, is vastly more effective at restoring growth than conventional hair loss treatments, though the design remains experimental.
 So far the technology has only been tested on mice, though the team from Beihang University in Beijing say the results suggest it would work to treat androgenetic alopecia, also known as male-pattern baldness, in humans. 
 open image in gallery The Detangle electric comb uses electrical pulses from the teeth to stimulate hair follicles ( Nature Communications ) The electronic comb was detailed in a study in the prestigious scientific journal Nature Communications this month.
 The study, titled ‘Combing-triggered electrostimulation synchronizing deep delivery for rapid hair regrowth in androgenetic alopecia’, revealed how the Detangled system was able to outperform minoxidil, the active ingredient in the popular hair loss treatment Rogaine.
 The Detangled comb features electronic teeth embedded with “height-differentiated electrodes and integrated drug-loading molecules” to generate an electric field in hair follicle regions.
 “The system significantly increases hair restoration efficacy in an androgenetic alopecia mouse model, improving outcome from ~70 per cent to nearly 100 per cent within one month compared to conventional topical minoxidil treatment,” the researchers wrote in the study .
 open image in gallery Male-pattern baldness impacts up to 80 per cent of men over their lifetimes ( Getty/iStock ) Male-pattern baldness is extremely common, impacting up to 80 per cent of men over their lifetimes.
 The condition can also come with psychological and quality-of-life impacts, but despite its prevalence, treatment options remain relatively limited.
 Minoxidil can be effective at slowing hair loss and encouraging regrowth, though results vary between individuals. It can also take up to a year to see any results and must be continued indefinitely to maintain the benefits.
 It can cause scalp irritation, while some users have also reported an increase in headaches while on the treatment.
 Another popular medication is finasteride, marketed as Propecia, which has proved effective during the early stages of baldness. Potential side effects, however, include erectile dysfunction and depression.
 More recently, hair transplantation has become increasingly popular, which involves removing follicles from areas of the scalp resistant to hair loss, such as the back and sides, and placing them on areas experiencing baldness. While effective, this treatment can be invasive, painful and costly.
 There is no evidence that the Detangle comb will work on humans, though testing on mice can serve as a benchmark for the effectiveness of treatments on humans.
 More tests will be required before clinical trials in humans can be conducted, which will aim to establish whether it is safe and effective.
